newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end down on correction.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end down on correction.

text.p: China's B and A share indices closed down on Wednesday on a correction triggered by the announcement of market expansion plans and the reaffirmation of a ban on domestic investors from buying B shares, brokers said.
In Shanghai, the B share index shed 2.162 points or 3.43 percent to close at 60.861 points, while Shenzhen's B share index fell 1.88 points or 1.32 percent to end at 140.27.
Shanghai brokers said market sentiment was hurt by news that 33 more companies had been chosen for B share listings and on a reaffirmation of the ban on domestic investors buying B shares.
"It will reduce the amount of capital in the market," one broker said.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai, whose 80 million B shares were listed today, also attracted capital away from other shares, brokers said.
Kaikai ended at $0.304, up 18.75 percent from its issue price of $0.256 on volume of 12.67 million shares, half the combined volume of 24.5 million shares on the Shanghai B share market.
Real estate developer Lujiazui performed poorly on selling by institutions, falling $0.040 or 4.62 percent to $0.826 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Meanwhile, Shenzhen's B share index closed down on a technical correction after strong rises in the previous session, brokers said.

They said Shenzhen's A and B stock indices were likely to continue to consolidate around current levels partly because institutions are unlikely to engage in large-scale trading unless there is major market-moving news.
Television maker Konka was the worst B share performer, losing HK$0.37 or 4.36 percent to HK$8.11 on thin volume of 77,481 shares due to speculative selling, brokers said.
The Shanghai A share market ended down modestly in sluggish trading on cautious sentiment, brokers said. The A index edged down 0.10 percent to 935.651 points.
Shanghai AJ lost the most on profit-taking, down 5.03 percent to 25.50 yuan.
The Shenzhen A share index slid 1.03 percent to close at 329.73 on a correction after gains on Tuesday.
Profit-taking sent market leader Shenzhen Development Bank down 0.53 yuan to 16.49 yuan on volume of 12.5 million shares, brokers said.
